title: Microimplantation of foreign materials for assessment of foreign body immune responses and granuloma formation in zebrafish larvae
protocol: Anesthetize larval zebrafish at 30–48 h post-fertilization by immersion in 0.02%w/v tricaine.
Add 630 μL of 0.4%w/v tricaine to 10 mL of fish water in a small 55 mm petri plate.
Transfer ≤100 larvae to the fish water containing tricaine using a wide-bore Pasteur pipette.
Incubate at room temperature for 3 min.
Transfer 10–20 larvae in approximately 1 mL of fish water containing tricaine to a depression slide.
Use the microprobe to group the larvae together at the nearest edge of the depression.
Implant larvae with foreign material.
Grasp a single larva by its tail using the VAMP.
Push the forebrain of the larva into the CAIN to make an incision.
Remove the larva from the CAIN by gently pulling with the VAMP.
Position the CAIN directly above the object to be implanted.
Lower the CAIN to grasp the object via capillary action.
Align the object with the incision in the forebrain.
Pass the object through the incision into the hindbrain ventricle.
Slightly angle the VAMP relative to the CAIN to wipe the object from the tip of the CAIN, depositing it into the hindbrain ventricle.
Repeat steps a-g until the desired number of larvae have been implanted.
Transfer implanted larvae into standard 100 mm petri plates containing 35 mL of fish water with 1× PTU.
House the larvae at a density no greater than 60 larvae per plate.
Incubate the larvae at 28°C for the desired amount of time before analysis.
Anesthetize larval zebrafish by immersion in 0.016%w/v tricaine.
Add 420 μL of 0.4%w/v tricaine to 10 mL of fish water in a petri plate.
Transfer ≤100 larvae to the fish water containing tricaine using a wide-bore Pasteur pipette.
Mount anesthetized larvae in 1.5% low melting point agarose.
Transfer 3–6 anesthetized larvae in approximately 20 μL of fish water to an optical glass-bottom plate with 20 mm glass diameter wells.
Add 20 μL of 1.5% low melting point agarose.
Swirl the larvae to mix the agar and fish water together using a microprobe.
Position the larvae laterally in a row.
Rotate the larvae to orient them with their hindbrain ventricle in contact with the bottom of the glass.
Reposition any larvae that rotate out of position before the agar solidifies.
Return the low melting point agarose to 43°C heat block.
Repeat steps until each well contains up to 36 mounted larvae.
Add 20 μL of fish water containing tricaine per group of 3–6 mounted larvae to prevent dehydration.
Fill the bottom of the well with fish water containing tricaine if imaging exceeds 1 hour.
Mount the plate of implanted zebrafish onto the stage of a confocal microscope.
Set X and Y coordinates for each larval hindbrain ventricle by eye, centering the implanted object in the field of view.
Under fluorescence, set the z position to 10 μm beyond the edge of each implanted object.
Set z-stack to scan through the depth of the implanted object with an additional 10 μm.
Set the imaging parameters for the desired resolution.
Click the “Run” button to start batch imaging of larvae automatically.
Analyze each image or timelapse video as needed for the experiment.
